key_insight: Droplet charge and vertical electric fields can accelerate collision-driven cloud droplet growth, potentially hastening warm rain initiation.
engineering_relevance: Charge- and field-dependent collision kernels could improve cloud microphysics models where electrostatic effects influence droplet growth.
method: Compute pair trajectories with droplet inertia, exact two-body hydrodynamics, electrostatics, and van der Waals forces.
Account for interfacial mobility and internal circulation in spherical, conducting droplets.
Evolve droplet mass and charge distributions using trajectory-derived collision kernels and a flux-method collection solver.
evidence_signal: For uncharged pairs with larger-droplet radii of 10 or 20 μm, increasing the field from 5×10⁴ to 3×10⁵ V/m can boost collision efficiency tenfold; at 40 minutes, every modeled electrified case produces a larger-radius large-droplet mass-spectrum mode than the hydrodynamic reference.
watch_item: Results assume still air and a uniform vertical field; applicability to turbulent clouds with spatially varying electrical conditions requires validation.
paper_title: Electrostatic effects on settling cloud droplets: from pair collisions to size distribution evolution
